formato: CourseGradingConfig.exam_script (apps/practice/conversa/exame.py, validar_guiao); carregar com manage.py carregar_exame_curso

perguntas.pergunta: Hello, {nome}. Welcome to your B1.2 speaking exam. What are you working on at the moment, at work or in your studies?
perguntas.simples: What are you doing at work these days?

perguntas.pergunta: Tell me about a phone call or a meeting you had recently. What did the other person say or ask?
perguntas.simples: Did you have an important call this week? What did they say?

perguntas.pergunta: What will you be doing this time next month? And what are you hoping to do next year?
perguntas.simples: What are your plans for next year?

perguntas.pergunta: Now I'd like you to talk for about one and a half minutes. Tell me about an incident or a problem you lived — at work, at school or at home. What happened, why did it happen, and what did you do? You can take a few seconds to think.
perguntas.simples: Tell me about a problem you had. What happened, and what did you do?

perguntas.pergunta: Thank you. Why do you think it happened? Could it have been avoided?
Looking back, what should you have done differently?

notas: Ask one question at a time and wait. Do not correct, teach or give hints during the exam.
If the student answers with one word or one short sentence, ask Can you tell me more? once per question.
In Part 2, let the student talk for about one and a half minutes without interrupting. If they stop after two or three sentences, ask And then what happened? once.
If the student does not work, ask about their studies, their home or a trip: a problem at school, a problem with a car, a lost bag.
In the situation, create the difficulty described in it once, so the student has to give a reason, a detail or a new solution.
After the situation, ask its discussion question, then give the opposite view once and ask the student to answer it. This is Part 4 (about 1 to 2 minutes).
If the student says That is an interesting question, What I mean is..., Sorry, I mean... or asks Do you mean...?, continue normally.
Use any B1 language, but no mixed conditionals, no wish or if only, and no passives with modals in the past.

tarefa.80-100: Answers every question with details; tells the story in a clear order, with causes and what was done; reports, summarises or explains with numbers in the situation, including the difficulty; answers the counter-argument with a reason.
tarefa.60-79: Answers most questions with some details; the story is clear, but the causes are short; completes the situation with some help; gives an opinion, but the answer to the counter-argument is short.
tarefa.40-59: Short answers; the story is hard to follow; the situation is only half done; no real answer to the counter-argument.
tarefa.0-39: Answers few questions, or answers in Portuguese.

gramatica.80-100: Chooses well among many tenses (narrative tenses with the past perfect, the future continuous); reports with reported speech; uses deduction, the third conditional and should have mostly correctly.
gramatica.60-79: Uses the B1.2 structures with some mistakes (for example She said me…, or would after if), but the meaning is always clear.
gramatica.40-59: Mostly A2 and B1.1 structures; frequent mistakes that sometimes make the meaning unclear.

vocabulario.80-100: Uses the words and collocations of B1 units 6-10 (incidents, calls, money and budgets, news, reviews) with ease, and explains words they do not know.
vocabulario.60-79: Enough words for the tasks; some pauses to find words; explains some missing words.
vocabulario.40-59: Basic work words are missing; the student often stops.
vocabulario.0-39: Very few words, or many Portuguese words.

fluencia.80-100: Long, organised turns with connectors (although, however, therefore, as a result, on the one hand); manages the conversation; few long pauses.
fluencia.60-79: Some long turns with connectors; pauses to organise ideas, but keeps going.
fluencia.40-59: Short, separate sentences and long pauses; needs help to continue.

nao_baixa: asking the examiner to repeat or to explain a question
saying That is an interesting question or Let me think to get time
pauses to organise ideas in the long turn
saying What I mean is... or In other words... to explain a word
correcting yourself with Sorry, I mean...
one wrong past participle when the structure is correct
